verdicts.note: Prolonged youth producing PROLONGED PARENTHOOD, and what that means for midlife parents. The parents'-side framing again; contact and support are the outcomes.
Childrearing and wellbeing cross-nationally.
Timing, sequencing and DURATION of youth-adult transitions in a Canadian cohort at 43, with LEAVING HOME as the first-stage marker. Duration is a measure the frame rarely carries.

Reproductive competition between CO-RESIDENT WOMEN in a historical population: simultaneous births reduce infant survival, and the paper asks whether that also lowers BIRTH RATES and whether women time pregnancies to avoid overlap. A co-residence-to-fertility estimate with an explicit scheduling mechanism -- and the co-residents are sisters-in-law, a configuration §6 does not name.
Social isolation and loneliness as public health risks.
Mother-son attachment predicting the daughter-in-law relationship and marital satisfaction in Turkey.
Sociocultural correlates of teenage pregnancy in the Philippines.

'Home-leaving and Parenthood': the TIMING OF LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME against the timing of first birth in Sweden, asking whether leaving at a younger or older age RELATIVE TO THE PREVAILING NORM predicts childbearing. The relative-to-norm construction is a partial answer to §3 -- it compares people against their cohort's schedule rather than against each other's realised sequence. Priority read.
Book review, a history of American teen bedrooms.
Social support and older adult health in China.
Filial piety and old-age support in China.

NON-CORESIDENT adult children's transitions to marriage and parenthood against contact frequency with parents. Parenthood is the exposure and contact the outcome -- the reverse of this chapter's arrow, in Korea.

Household composition across 13 ASIAN countries, 1980-2010, census and survey combined, with CO-RESIDENCE WITH PARENTS traced over the life course at the individual level. The best exposure-trend record in the frame for the extended arm's region.
Family structure and co-residence in a bargaining model of women's EMPOWERMENT in Pakistan. Arrangement as exposure, empowerment as outcome.
Chapter on marital transitions including the launching of children.
Daughters-in-law with disabilities and their relations with parents-in-law, including when they live together.

Thesis on FERTILITY AND FAMILY TIES, comparing NORWAY AND SPAIN -- the weak-ties and strong-ties poles of the registered mechanism -- with partnership type among the channels. Two-country contrast, so Wall 3 binds; trace the chapters for a within-country design.
Pittsburgh ACS household-type data record.
No abstract; preprint of the clan-culture family-support paper.
Children living with parents who have a substance use disorder.
No abstract; the Journal of Comparative Economics version of the gated anchor 'Fertility, household structure, and parental labor supply: Evidence from China'. Keep this over the SSRN preprint.

Argues fertility theories should be embedded in more realistic theories of HOUSEHOLD FORMATION and intrahousehold bargaining, with evidence that partners disagree about fertility. The theoretical case for this chapter's estimand, and for why the extended arm's in-law records matter.

IDENTIFIED, AND THE BEST WALL-1 RECORD YET. Exploits regional US house-price variation in the 2000s boom against young Americans' HOME OWNERSHIP, HOUSEHOLD FORMATION and FERTILITY, with a NOVEL INSTRUMENT built on predetermined industrial structure. All three outcomes in one instrumented design -- it can decompose how much of the price effect on fertility runs through household formation, which is exactly the non-additivity question §2 inherited from C.2.c and could not answer. Priority read; second-read packet.
Cultural variables in Soviet immigrants' fertility in Israel. D.1.b's.
Historical essay on parenthood as necessity in the ancient world.
Borsodi and decentralist economics.
Concluding chapter of an Asian population handbook.
Folklore study of swan-maiden tales; matrilocal versus patrilocal marriage appears as a motif.
Chapter on reparations for state-sponsored reproductive deprivation.
Book version of 'The Boomerang Age'; the pre-launch exposure trend as a monograph.
Introduction to a volume on young adults' family-related transitions and the decline of a standard sequence.
Microsimulation of HIV/AIDS demographic impact in Nigeria.
Fertility as an adjustment to mortality risk. A.1's.
No abstract; parental responses to child support obligations from administrative data. Identified, but the exposure is a transfer obligation and the outcome is not the arrangement.
Editorial on ageing with haemophilia.
No abstract; clan culture as a substitute for social support. Published version of the preprint above.
No abstract; gender differences in intergenerational care-giving and migration.

No abstract; women's INHERITANCE RIGHTS REFORM and son preference in India. An identified legal reform, but the exposure is inheritance rights and the outcome son preference. D.2.c's -- though inheritance reform plausibly moves patrilocal residence, which would make it a design-6 candidate; note for §4.

EXTENDED HOUSEHOLDS in CHILE analysed as SUBFAMILIES -- about a quarter of households 1990-2011, and NOT declining despite other family change. Latin America, and the subfamily unit is the measurement §9 needs for distinguishing a couple within a parental household.
Male fertility patterns in the Czech Republic; structural and situational variables.

'SUBSIDIZED HOUSING AND THE TRANSITION TO ADULTHOOD' in Demography: the effect of the US federal subsidised-housing programme on HOW AND WHEN children become adults. Scope §4 design 3 -- administrative allocation of dwellings -- realised in a peer-reviewed demography journal, in the arm that has almost no identified evidence. Priority read.
Gender gaps in political engagement across four life-course stages including HOME-LEAVING and the empty nest, 27 countries. Arrangement as a stage, politics as outcome.
Parents' positivity and negativity toward children following transitions tied to RESIDENCE, unions and parenthood. Parents'-side outcome.
No abstract; historic roots of quality of government and gender equality.

Swedish REGISTER studies on parental leave and CO-RESIDENCE around the transition to parenthood and separation. Register data on co-residence is the measurement quality §9 wants; the outcomes here are gender inequality and separation.
LEAVING HOME among four early-adulthood transitions against changes in diet. Arrangement as exposure, diet as outcome.
Transitions surrounding CO-RESIDENCE and parenthood against sibling relationship quality.

Reconceptualising THREE-GENERATION CO-RESIDENCE in post-growth Japan, noting that pension income and savings made ageing parents financially independent -- so the arrangement's meaning changed even where its prevalence did not. A caution for any trend series that treats co-residence as one construct over time.
Living alone in later life, global perspective. The homonym, and one of the frame's most-cited records.
Maternal burnout syndrome.

Conversation with and support from PARENTS AND PARENTS-IN-LAW, separately from husband and siblings, against FERTILITY INTENTIONS of Korean married women with at least one child. Panel data, and it separates the natal from the affinal side -- the distinction §6's configuration split needs and most records collapse.
Psychological distress among childless versus coresident and noncoresident older Thais.
Preconception care awareness among family members of women with type 1 diabetes.
Oral history of Kalmyk wedding ritual.
Caregiving intentions of China's one-child generation toward parents and parents-in-law.
